lens.message:
Here's the shift: a submission that arrives without an explicit id is no longer an unspecified edge case — it's now a standing requirement that the system derive the identifier itself (LLM id-gen first, deterministic slugify fallback behind it) and commit the file successfully every time. The fallback is the guarantee: a missing id can never block a memory from landing.

What it changes our approach to: submissions lacking an explicit id (expected input, not an error), the handoff from the id-gen call to the deterministic slugify fallback (a required backstop, not a convenience), and what counts as a failed commit (a missing id no longer qualifies).

As written, in this memory: "Submitted without an explicit id field. The pipeline must produce a slug from the memory content — either via the LLM id-gen call or the deterministic slugify fallback — and commit the file successfully."

Read through the shift: "must" binds the whole ingest — if the id-gen call comes back empty, the deterministic slugify takes over and the file still commits. A submission without an id is an expected input, and the fallback exists precisely so the commit succeeds; there's no reading where the submission is turned away for lacking one.
